Apple___Apple_scab.name: Apple Scab
Apple___Apple_scab.description: A common fungal disease that causes dark, scabby lesions on leaves and fruit, reducing fruit quality and weakening trees.
symptoms: Olive-green to brown velvety spots on leaves
Leaves curl, yellow and drop early
causes: Infected fallen leaves that overwinter the fungus
Poor air circulation in dense canopies

organic: Spray sulfur or lime-sulfur at green-tip through petal fall
Apply copper soap early in the season
chemical: Captan or mancozeb protectant sprays every 7-10 days in wet weather
Myclobutanil or difenoconazole for curative action within 48-72 h of infection
cultural: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn
Apply urea (5%) to fallen leaves to speed decomposition

prevention: Begin protective sprays at bud break

Apple___Black_rot.name: Black Rot
Apple___Black_rot.description: A fungal disease causing leaf spots ('frog-eye'), fruit rot and limb cankers on apple trees.
symptoms: Purple-edged leaf spots with tan centres (frog-eye)
causes: Infected mummified fruit and dead wood
Wounds from pruning, insects or hail

organic: Prune out cankers 15 cm below visible damage
chemical: Captan or thiophanate-methyl from petal fall through summer
Combine with scab spray program
cultural: Remove dead wood and fire-blight strikes

prevention: Keep trees vigorous with balanced fertilisation
Remove nearby wild or abandoned apple trees

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.name: Cedar Apple Rust
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: A rust fungus that alternates between apple and juniper/cedar hosts, causing bright orange leaf spots.
symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on upper leaf surface
causes: Nearby juniper or red cedar trees carrying galls

organic: Sulfur sprays from pink bud through early summer
chemical: Myclobutanil or fenarimol at 7-10 day intervals during spore release
cultural: Remove junipers within a few hundred metres where practical

prevention: Inspect junipers for galls in late winter

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.name: Powdery Mildew
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.description: A fungal disease producing white powdery growth on leaves and shoots, reducing photosynthesis and fruit quality.
symptoms: Leaves curl upward and become distorted

organic: Milk spray (1:9 with water) for light infections
chemical: Myclobutanil, trifloxystrobin or quinoxyfen
Rotate fungicide groups to prevent resistance
cultural: Prune to improve light and airflow

prevention: Begin sprays at first sign of disease

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.name: Gray Leaf Spot
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: A foliar disease producing rectangular grey lesions that can severely reduce yield in humid regions.
symptoms: Narrow, rectangular tan-to-grey lesions bounded by leaf veins
Lesions merge and blight entire leaves
causes: Corn residue left on the surface
Prolonged leaf wetness and high humidity

organic: Remove and destroy heavily infected lower leaves
chemical: Strobilurin (azoxystrobin, pyraclostrobin) or triazole fungicides at tasseling
Premixes such as azoxystrobin + propiconazole
cultural: Rotate with non-host crops for 1-2 years
Till under residue where erosion is not a concern

prevention: Avoid dense planting in humid fields

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.name: Common Rust
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: A rust disease producing cinnamon-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces.
symptoms: Pustules on both upper and lower leaf surfaces
Leaves yellow and die in severe cases

organic: Remove heavily infected leaves in small plots
chemical: Triazole (propiconazole, tebuconazole) or strobilurin fungicides when pustules first appear
cultural: Plant early to avoid peak spore periods

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.name: Northern Leaf Blight
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: A fungal disease producing long, cigar-shaped grey-green lesions that can cause significant yield loss.
symptoms: Lesions turn tan with dark spore patches
causes: Moderate temperatures (18-27 °C) with long dew periods

chemical: Azoxystrobin, propiconazole or pyraclostrobin at first lesion appearance before tasseling

prevention: Plant hybrids with Ht resistance genes

Grape___Black_rot.name: Black Rot
Grape___Black_rot.description: A destructive fungal disease of grapes that can destroy an entire crop in warm, wet seasons.
symptoms: Small brown circular leaf spots with dark borders
Berries shrivel into hard black mummies
causes: Warm, rainy weather from bloom to veraison

organic: Copper or sulfur sprays from early shoot growth
chemical: Mancozeb, myclobutanil or captan from bud break to 4 weeks after bloom

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).name: Esca (Black Measles)
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: A trunk disease complex causing 'tiger-stripe' leaf symptoms, berry spotting and gradual vine decline.
causes: Fungi entering through large pruning wounds

organic: Protect pruning wounds with Trichoderma-based paste
chemical: No curative chemical; seal pruning wounds with fungicidal wound sealant (e.g. thiophanate-methyl paste)
cultural: Trunk renewal by training a new shoot from below the infection
Prune in dry weather and late in dormancy

prevention: Double pruning to reduce wound exposure

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.name: Leaf Blight (Isariopsis Leaf Spot)
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.description: A foliar disease producing irregular dark brown spots that may cause premature defoliation.
symptoms: Irregular dark red-brown spots on leaves
Spots coalesce into large blighted areas

organic: Copper oxychloride or Bordeaux mixture sprays
chemical: Mancozeb or carbendazim at 10-14 day intervals

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).name: Huanglongbing (Citrus Greening)
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).pathogen: Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus (spread by Asian citrus psyllid)
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: A devastating, incurable bacterial disease that causes blotchy mottled leaves, misshapen bitter fruit and eventual tree death.
symptoms: Asymmetrical blotchy yellow mottling on leaves
Small, lopsided, bitter fruit that stays green
causes: Transmission by Asian citrus psyllid (Diaphorina citri)

organic: Control psyllids with neem oil, horticultural oil or kaolin clay
Release natural enemies such as Tamarixia radiata
chemical: Systemic insecticides (imidacloprid, thiamethoxam) for psyllid control
No cure: remove and destroy confirmed infected trees
cultural: Enhanced nutrition programs to prolong productivity
Report suspected cases to local agricultural authorities

Peach___Bacterial_spot.name: Bacterial Spot
Peach___Bacterial_spot.description: A bacterial disease causing leaf spots, defoliation and pitted, cracked fruit.
symptoms: Small water-soaked spots that turn purple-brown
Spots fall out leaving shot holes

organic: Copper sprays at leaf fall and bud swell
chemical: Oxytetracycline sprays during the growing season
Low-rate copper during the season (watch for leaf burn)
cultural: Maintain tree vigour with proper fertilisation

prevention: Avoid planting on light sandy soils exposed to wind

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.name: Bacterial Spot
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.description: A bacterial disease producing leaf lesions and scabby fruit spots; spreads rapidly in warm rainy weather.
symptoms: Small water-soaked spots that turn brown with yellow halos

chemical: Copper + mancozeb tank mix
Acibenzolar-S-methyl to induce plant resistance

prevention: Rotate away from peppers/tomatoes for 2-3 years

Potato___Early_blight.name: Early Blight
Potato___Early_blight.description: A common fungal disease producing target-like concentric leaf spots, mainly on older leaves.
symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings (target pattern)

organic: Bacillus subtilis or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens biofungicides
chemical: Chlorothalonil or mancozeb every 7-10 days
Azoxystrobin or difenoconazole for heavier pressure

prevention: Water at the base in the morning

Potato___Late_blight.name: Late Blight
Potato___Late_blight.description: A fast-spreading, highly destructive disease (cause of the Irish potato famine) that can destroy entire fields within days.
symptoms: Large dark water-soaked lesions on leaves
White fuzzy growth on leaf undersides in humid conditions
causes: Infected seed tubers and cull piles

organic: Immediately remove and bag infected plants (do not compost)
chemical: Chlorothalonil or mancozeb protectants
Systemic products such as cymoxanil, metalaxyl-M or mandipropamid at first sign
cultural: Destroy volunteer potatoes and cull piles
Kill vines 2-3 weeks before harvest to protect tubers

Squash___Powdery_mildew.name: Powdery Mildew
Squash___Powdery_mildew.description: A very common fungal disease covering cucurbit leaves with white powder, reducing yield and fruit quality.
symptoms: White powdery spots on upper and lower leaf surfaces
causes: Warm dry days with humid nights

organic: Potassium bicarbonate, sulfur or neem oil sprays
chemical: Myclobutanil, trifloxystrobin or chlorothalonil
Rotate fungicide classes

prevention: Start preventive sprays when conditions favour disease

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.name: Leaf Scorch
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.description: A fungal disease causing purple blotches that merge until leaves look scorched.
symptoms: Small irregular purple spots on upper leaf surface
Spots merge; leaf margins dry and look burnt

organic: Remove and destroy infected leaves after harvest
chemical: Captan or myclobutanil from early bloom

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.name: Bacterial Spot
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: A bacterial disease causing small dark leaf spots, defoliation and scabby fruit lesions.
symptoms: Small dark water-soaked spots on leaves
Spots with yellow halos that may fall out
Raised scabby spots on green fruit
causes: Warm, wet weather and splashing water

chemical: Copper + mancozeb combination
Acibenzolar-S-methyl as plant defence activator
cultural: Do not handle plants when wet

Tomato___Early_blight.name: Early Blight
Tomato___Early_blight.description: A widespread fungal disease producing target-like spots on older leaves and stem lesions.
symptoms: Brown lesions with concentric rings on lower leaves
Dark sunken spots at fruit stem end
causes: Spores in soil and plant debris

chemical: Chlorothalonil or mancozeb every 7-10 days
Azoxystrobin or difenoconazole for severe infections

prevention: Rotate crops (avoid solanaceous crops for 3 years)

Tomato___Late_blight.name: Late Blight
Tomato___Late_blight.description: An aggressive disease that can kill tomato plants within a week in cool, wet weather.
symptoms: Large greasy grey-green to brown blotches on leaves
causes: Airborne spores from nearby infected potatoes or tomatoes

organic: Remove and bag infected plants immediately
chemical: Chlorothalonil or mancozeb protectants
Mandipropamid, cymoxanil or famoxadone for active infections

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.name: Leaf Mold
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: A fungal disease mainly in greenhouses and high tunnels, favoured by high humidity.
symptoms: Pale green-yellow spots on upper leaf surface
Olive-green to brown velvety mould underneath

chemical: Chlorothalonil, mancozeb or difenoconazole
cultural: Heat and vent greenhouse in the evening to reduce condensation

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.name: Septoria Leaf Spot
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: A fungal disease producing many small circular spots that cause heavy defoliation.
symptoms: Numerous small round spots with dark borders and grey centres
Tiny black specks (pycnidia) in spot centres

chemical: Chlorothalonil or mancozeb every 7-10 days

prevention: Clean up debris at season end

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.name: Two-spotted Spider Mite
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Tiny sap-sucking mites that cause stippled, bronzed leaves and fine webbing, especially in hot dry weather.
symptoms: Fine yellow or white stippling on leaves
causes: Overuse of broad-spectrum insecticides killing natural predators

organic: Strong water spray to dislodge mites
chemical: Miticides such as abamectin, bifenazate or spiromesifen
Rotate miticide groups

Tomato___Target_Spot.name: Target Spot
Tomato___Target_Spot.description: A fungal disease causing concentric ringed lesions on leaves, stems and fruit.
symptoms: Brown lesions with concentric rings and light centres

chemical: Chlorothalonil, azoxystrobin or difenoconazole

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.name: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: A viral disease transmitted by whiteflies that stunts plants and drastically reduces yield. There is no cure.
symptoms: Upward curling and cupping of leaves

organic: Neem oil or insecticidal soap for whitefly control
chemical: Systemic insecticides (imidacloprid, cyantraniliprole) for whitefly control
No chemical cure for the virus itself

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.name: Tomato Mosaic Virus
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: A highly stable, mechanically transmitted virus causing mottled leaves and reduced yields. There is no cure.
symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic mottling

organic: Disinfect tools with 10% bleach or milk solution
chemical: No chemical cure available

Generic___Leaf_spot_or_blight.name: Leaf Spot / Blight (general)
Generic___Leaf_spot_or_blight.pathogen: Various fungi or bacteria (e.g. Alternaria, Septoria, Xanthomonas)
Generic___Leaf_spot_or_blight.description: Brown or black necrotic lesions consistent with a fungal or bacterial leaf spot or blight.
symptoms: Brown or black spots or patches

chemical: Broad-spectrum protectant such as chlorothalonil or mancozeb

Generic___Powdery_mildew.name: Powdery Mildew (general)
Generic___Powdery_mildew.description: White powdery coating on the leaf surface typical of powdery mildew.

organic: Potassium bicarbonate, sulfur or neem oil sprays
chemical: Myclobutanil or trifloxystrobin

Generic___Rust.name: Rust (general)
Generic___Rust.description: Orange to reddish-brown pustules or spots characteristic of rust fungi.

chemical: Triazole fungicides (propiconazole, tebuconazole, myclobutanil)

Generic___Chlorosis_or_viral_yellowing.name: Chlorosis / Yellowing
Generic___Chlorosis_or_viral_yellowing.pathogen: Nutrient deficiency (N, Fe, Mg) or viral infection
Generic___Chlorosis_or_viral_yellowing.description: Widespread yellowing of leaf tissue, which may indicate nutrient deficiency, root problems or a viral infection.
causes: High soil pH locking out iron

organic: Apply compost or balanced organic fertiliser
chemical: Balanced NPK fertiliser
Control insect vectors (aphids, whiteflies) if viral
cultural: Remove plants with confirmed viral symptoms
